correctness.rationale: For odd \(q\), the commutator is \([a,b]=2a_{\mathrm{odd}}b_{\mathrm{odd}}\), and only the exterior-degree-two and exterior-degree-four wedge terms survive modulo \(J^5\). Decomposing by vanishing of the degree-one components gives exactly \(q^{2h}+(q^n-1)(q+1)q^{2h-r}\) commuting odd-component pairs, where \(r=\binom{n-1}{3}\). Multiplication by the arbitrary even components yields the asserted commuting probability. The strict six-generator majority threshold follows from \(r\le n-1\) for \(n\le5\) and \(r\ge n+4\) thereafter, valid for every odd prime power \(q\ge3\). In the full five-generator exterior algebra, nonzero degree-one wedge multiplication has rank eight; when the degree-one part vanishes, cubic wedge multiplication is dual to a five-dimensional alternating form with ranks zero, two and four. The standard rank-fiber counts supply all centralizer multiplicities. Independently implemented wedge-product matrices and direct finite-field rank enumerations in `verify.py` corroborate the critical finite identities. The general proof is algebraic and characteristic two is excluded.

value.rationale: Ordinary commuting probability is a canonical finite-ring invariant, and the fourth augmentation-ideal truncation is the first natural exterior-jet level with linear–cubic odd coupling. The exact formula for every \(n\ge1\) detects a strict majority reversal between \(n=5\) and \(n=6\), uniformly over all odd finite fields, which the generic supercommutation rule alone does not count. The full five-generator centralizer enumerator resolves the first rank where cubic odd forms have two nonzero wedge ranks, giving a complete natural finite-algebra spectrum rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. These results can inform commuting-graph and centralizer-statistics comparisons; no external certification or downstream theorem is asserted.
